# Jabbit - Peptide Tracking App
> Jabbit is an iPhone app for people who take GLP-1 medications or other injectable peptides. It logs doses and injection sites, tracks vials and reconstitution, estimates medication levels, and records progress. No account; data syncs through the user's own iCloud. Made by Bridger Apps, LLC.

## Key Features
- Smart injection tracking with 14-zone site rotation
- Vial management with reconstitution calculator
- Real-time serum level visualization (pharmacokinetic curves)
- Flexible dosing schedules (daily, EOD, 2x/week, 5-on-2-off, custom)
- Titration and cycle planning
- Progress tracking with Apple Health sync
- In-app encyclopedia of peptides with half-life data
- Privacy-first: iCloud sync only, no server storage

## Pricing (US App Store, as of October 2026)
- Free download with a 14-day free trial
- Then $9.99/year (the App Store lists one in-app purchase, "Jabbit Pro", at $9.99)
- iPhone app (iOS 17 or later; the listing says it also runs on iPad); no Android app

## Study Teardowns
Critical single-study reads: design, comparator, funding, dropout, effect size, enrollment, and durability, with charts rebuilt from published numbers.
- Study teardowns hub: https://jabbitapp.com/research
- Do ivermectin and mebendazole treat cancer? The Oct 19, 2026 McCullough/Wellness Company review, checked (pegged to the Zenodo preprint by Hulscher, Thorp, Victory, Gillooly, McCullough and Risch and an X trending story; Jabbit Crossref check of all 138 cited DOIs: 4 cited works retracted (2 disclosed), 1 under an editorial expression of concern (npj Breast Cancer 2021 ivermectin 'cold tumors hot' mouse study, undisclosed); of the review's 3 'positive' human studies, METRICS (glioblastoma, 4-drug) was retracted Oct 13, 2026 (Frontiers' notice says the MHRA found it was a clinical trial conducted without appropriate ethics approval or informed consent; METRICS was not run by the review's authors), and the authors' own 197-person TWC customer survey (84.4% self-reported benefit) was retracted Oct 1, 2026 (no misconduct alleged; authors dispute); the remaining Hegazy 2022 mebendazole trial (40 people) is listed on ClinicalTrials.gov (entry last updated April 2019) as open-label with an active comparator and recruiting, unlike the paper's double-blind placebo description, and by Jabbit's cross-trial comparison its control arm (PFS 3.0 months, ORR 10%) did worse than bevacizumab + FOLFOX4 benchmarks (NO16966 9.4 months; E3200 7.3 months, 22.7%); by Jabbit's estimate from the label, ivermectin's 5 uM lab dose is about 94x the Stromectol 12 mg mean peak (46.6 ng/mL, 0.053 uM), about 9x short at 120 mg if dose-proportional; mebendazole lab IC50 0.11-0.31 uM vs label max 0.10 uM; 0 of 9 registered ivermectin/mebendazole anticancer trials have results and none tests the pair; the review's conflict statement says all authors 'are affiliated with and/or receive salary support from The Wellness Company (TWC)'; TWC's site listed 25 mg + 250 mg capsules at $599.99/90 on Oct 20, 2026): https://jabbitapp.com/research/ivermectin-mebendazole-cancer-review-retractions-evidence.html

- Stopped losing weight on Ozempic, Wegovy, Zepbound or Mounjaro? Why plateaus happen, and whether a higher dose, tirzepatide or retatrutide helps (Oct 20, 2026; pegged to Medscape's Oct 20 "Could Retatrutide Break a GLP-1 Weight-Loss Plateau?" and TRIUMPH-1 in NEJM, Sept 29; plateau timing: median 24.3-36.1 weeks on tirzepatide in SURMOUNT-1, 87.6-90.2% plateaued by week 72 (Lilly post hoc); appetite feedback about 100 kcal/day per kg lost, more than 3x the energy-expenditure drop; staying on after a plateau: STEP 4 -7.9% vs +6.9%, SURMOUNT-4 -5.5% vs +14.0%; higher dose: STEP UP semaglutide 7.2 mg -18.7% vs 2.4 mg -15.6%, dysaesthesia 22.9% vs 6.0%; SURMOUNT-5 tirzepatide -20.2% vs semaglutide -13.7%; Weill Cornell switchers to tirzepatide +8.1% after a plateau vs +2.9% for non-responders at 6 months; TRIUMPH-1 retatrutide 12 mg -25.0% (treatment-regimen) vs -28.3% (efficacy estimand); Jabbit label scan: 0 of 9 US labels mention plateau, only Wegovy has a step-up-for-more-weight-loss rule, only Saxenda a stop rule; Jabbit ClinicalTrials.gov review: 22 'what next' studies, 3 with results; 33 retatrutide intervention studies, none built for people coming off semaglutide or tirzepatide, 16 exclude recent weight-loss drugs incl. all nine TRIUMPH phase 3 trials): https://jabbitapp.com/research/ozempic-wegovy-zepbound-weight-loss-plateau-retatrutide-switch.html
